findings.quote_pt: Não é que o sistema não tenha memória de sessão relevante; é que a ingestão dessa família parou há três semanas, e a janela do sub-pool é de uma. **Metade do canal de cobertura está inerte por idade, não por desenho.**
findings.problem: Relative time ('há três semanas', as of 2026-08-30) plus a cause that was established later. Session ingestion produced 0 chunks from 2026-08-11 to 2026-09-07 because a VPS migration moved the address and schema of the transcripts (cron reported ok). ALL ingestion was frozen from 2026-08-24 01:06:35 to 2026-09-07 14:06:13Z by a watcher calling a missing binary. So the 108-chunk pool, its exhaustion on 26–29/08 and the 'five days with zero new items' were all measured inside a broken-ingestion regime. After the repair, per-agent eligibles were 219 -> 285 (2026-09-09).
findings.proposed_en: It is not that the system lacks relevant session memory: on 2026-08-30 the newest such chunk was 20.5 days old, and the sub-pool's window is 7 days. **We later established why** (`DEVIATIONS-FOR-PAPER.md` §10.5, §10.7). A host migration had moved both the address and the schema of the agents' session transcripts, and session ingestion produced zero chunks from 2026-08-11 until it was repaired on 2026-09-07, while its cron reported `ok`. Separately, all ingestion was frozen from 2026-08-24 01:06Z to 2026-09-07 14:06Z by a watcher invoking a missing binary. Half of the coverage channel was therefore inert **because of an ingestion defect, not by design and not because of the normal cadence of ingestion**. After the repair, the per-agent sub-pool held 285 eligible chunks (2026-09-09). Every coverage-channel number in this section was measured inside that broken regime: the 108-chunk pool, its daily exhaustion on 26–29/08, and the five days without new items. They describe the channel under defective ingestion, not its steady state.
findings.evidence: DEVIATIONS-FOR-PAPER.md §10.5 (l.562-580: MAX(created_at)=2026-08-24 01:06:35 until 2026-09-07T14:06:13Z, 0 chunks 08-25..09-06, nox-mem-watch.sh missing binary) and §10.7 (l.715-728: sessions/% 0 chunks 2026-08-11..09-07, migration of address+schema, repaired 09-07); docs/HANDOFF.md 2026-09-09 (agent_fresh_elegiveis 219 -> 285); grep -n -i 'congel|watch|08-24|distill|migra' MANUSCRIPT.md -> no mention of either defect.

findings.quote_pt: `JOIN chunks` faz 20/08 aparecer com 33 distintos onde `brief_log` diz 85 — os outros **52 não existem mais** (servidos e apagados depois).
findings.problem: Wrong day. Measured per UTC day, and identically per BRT day: 20/08 = 87 distinct with 35 surviving the JOIN, 21/08 = 85 with 33, 22/08 = 193 with 141. The pair 85/33 belongs to 21/08. All three days lose the same 52 chunks. Also, 'servidos e apagados depois' is only partly true: 966 of their 2,600 slots were served after the chunks had already been deleted from the main DB. The 85/33 figure had no artifact; it came only from a docstring in regime-cobertura.py, lines 23-25.
findings.proposed_en: ⚠️ **A counting trap, recorded because it nearly caught us.** Counting exposure with `JOIN chunks` makes 21/08 show 33 distinct chunks where `brief_log` says 85. The other **52 no longer exist**. The same 52 vanish from 20/08 (87 → 35) and 22/08 (193 → 141). They are one ingestion of `memory/lessons.md` (ids 308114–308165), replaced by a re-ingest on 2026-08-22 02:01:58 UTC, and the serving path kept handing them out for about 17 h afterwards (966 of their 2,600 slots). Exposure counts come from `brief_log`; only what needs chunk metadata uses the JOIN, and it declares the loss.
findings.evidence: _sprint-2026-10-04/A-recon/RECON-52-e-sondas-2026-10-04.json → c52.por_dia_utc, c52.identidade_no_pre_db, c52.servidos_depois_da_substituicao=[966,483]; produced by measurement/sprint-recon-52-e-sondas.py on copies of e20260907T060001Z.db (sha256 4ec7e182…, which matches p2-bancos-ensaio.sha256), daily-main 20260821060004 (gunzipped copy, sha256 40683f8e…) and pre-op kg-confirm-main-20260822020237 (sha256 fba69260…). The BRT grouping was checked with a separate sqlite3 query on the same copy.

findings.quote_pt: ⚠️ E o número **52** aparece duas vezes nesta seção sobre populações diferentes: um único dia (`20/08`, 85 distintos → 33 sobrevivem ao JOIN) e a **semana inteira** (201 → 149) têm ambos 52 apagados. Ou é o mesmo conjunto — e então toda a poda da semana concentra num dia, que é um facto a reportar — ou é coincidência de calendário **não conferida** [...] Não a conferimos; fica declarada (2026-09-21, por revisão adversarial). São os mesmos 201; **52 foram apagados desde então**
findings.problem: The reconciliation is now measured and both branches of the dilemma are false. The week's missing set is set-equal to the missing set of each of 20/08, 21/08 and 22/08. It is one coverage-channel batch served over about 46 h across three days, so it is neither a one-day concentration nor a coincidence. The paragraph also contradicts itself: it says 'Não a conferimos' and then asserts 'São os mesmos 201'.
findings.proposed_en: ⚠️ **The population of the counterfactual is 149, while §4.3 counts 201 distinct chunks in the same window. The 52 missing are one identified set, not a coincidence.** As sets, the 52 absent from the week (201 → 149) are exactly the 52 absent from each of 20/08, 21/08 and 22/08. They are ids 308114–308165: one ingestion of `memory/lessons.md` (`lesson`, created 2026-08-20 02:02:03 UTC), served only by the coverage channel (2 per brief, 1,300 briefs, all six agents) from 20/08 21:38 to 22/08 19:07 UTC. The file was re-ingested on 22/08 02:01:58 UTC and the 52 were replaced by 53 new chunks. All 53 replacements were served in the window and are among the 149. A deleted chunk has no `importance`, `pain` or `access_count` to recompute salience from, so the 149-chunk recompute leaves them out. The 52 were restored from a backup taken while they existed; the result is below.
findings.evidence: RECON-52-e-sondas-2026-10-04.json → c52.por_dia_utc[*].ausentes_igual_ao_conjunto_da_semana (true for 20, 21 and 22/08), c52.ausentes_ids_min_max=[308114,308165], ausentes_contiguos=true, ausentes_servidos{primeiro 2026-08-20 21:38:47, ultimo 2026-08-22 19:07:46, slots 2600, briefs 1300, linhas_por_brief {2:1300}}, linhagem_do_arquivo (pre 52 ids @2026-08-20 02:02:03; post and serving 53 ids 308444–308496 @2026-08-22 02:01:58), substitutos_servidos_na_janela=[53,53]

findings.quote_pt: 128–131 é um **limite inferior** para a queda — sobre o pool completo os três cairiam igual ou mais. Quanto mais, não medimos, e fica declarado.
findings.problem: This can now be measured, and it was. The published 149-chunk result reproduces exactly (2/131, 3/129, 5/128) on the epoch copy at three pinned 'now' values on 2026-08-29. Restoring the 52 from the 2026-08-21 backup gives 183/181/180 on the full 201. Probe-only chunks also sit inside the 149; see the 25-slot finding.
findings.proposed_en: So 128–131 is a **lower bound** on the drop. It is now measured on the full pool: with the 52 deleted chunks restored from a backup taken while they existed (2026-08-21 06:00 UTC), and zeroing the access term, the three fall to **183, 181 and 180 of 201**. That is exactly 52 places lower, since every restored chunk outranks them. One caveat: the 52 are earlier versions of `lessons.md` whose replacements are already among the 149, so the 201-pool counts that content twice; it is nonetheless the population that was served. Excluding our five health probes (§4.3) the figures are 126/124/123 of 144 and 178/176/175 of 196. Every variant leaves the three beyond rank 100.
findings.evidence: RECON-52-e-sondas-2026-10-04.json → contrafactual.rodadas[0..2] (posicoes_149 equal to artefato_publicado; posicoes_201 = 183/181/180; identical for now = 2026-08-29 00:00:00, 12:00:00 and 23:59:59); ORGANICO-e-hashes-2026-10-04.txt → posicoes_144, posicoes_196. The access_count of the 3 in the epoch copy (911/414/363) equals out/TOP-COUNTERFACTUAL-2026-08-29.json.

findings.quote_pt: 🔑 **Declarado como hipótese, não como facto:** a igualdade `25 = 5 × 5` é exata, mas não confirmámos a identidade das cinco sondas dentro desta janela de 7 dias — só que `ancora-sondas.json` lista cinco. [...] A reconciliação fica **aberta**
findings.problem: Now confirmed by identity. In the window, the brief-size histogram is {10 rows: 4,627 briefs, 5 rows: 5 briefs}, with 0 NULL brief_ids. The 5 short briefs' brief_ids equal ancora-sondas.json sondas_excluidas as a set.
findings.proposed_en: 🔑 **Confirmed by identity, not only by arithmetic.** The window holds exactly 5 briefs that do not have 10 rows. Each has 5 rows; the other 4,627 all have 10, and no row lacks a `brief_id`. Their `brief_id`s are, as a set, the five that `out/ancora-sondas.json` lists as `sondas_excluidas`. All are `scope=global` with no agent, issued on 2026-08-26 at 19:58:17–18 and 20:28:55–56 UTC. So the 4,632 briefs **do** include our five health probes, and `25 = 5 × 5` is an identity. The probes are also not neutral to the distinct count. Each carries the three constants plus two other chunks, and five of those chunks (307967–307970 from `memory/decisions.md`, 308443 from `memory/projects.md`) were served exactly once ever, inside a probe. Without the probes the window has **46,270 slots in 4,627 briefs and 196 distinct chunks**. Top-10 and top-20 shares are unchanged (47.16%, 61.46%), and the same 3 chunks appear in 100% of briefs. The contradiction with §2 remains textual: *"always 10 items"* is false for exactly these five probe briefs.

⚠️ **O artefato cobre UM dia, e a afirmação abaixo cobre quatro.** Verificado em
2026-09-21 por revisão adversarial: ... **um artefato citado para sustentar mais do que contém**.
findings.problem: The warning describes a gap that has now been closed by re-measurement from preserved data. Keeping it unchanged would misstate the current evidentiary status. It should become a short history note that says how the gap was closed.
findings.proposed_en: ⚠️ **Until 2026-10-04 the artifact covered ONE day while the claim covered four.** Adversarial review on 2026-09-21 found that `POOL-ELEGIVEL-2026-08-28.json` holds only 2026-08-28. The other three days had been measured by the same route and not preserved. The review suspected in-place rewriting; there was none, because the file on disk is identical to the versioned one. The gap was closed by re-measuring from a preserved trial database (`corpus-SERVING-REAL-e20260903-recuperado.db`, sha256-verified copy) using the same predicate. A positive control came first: re-running 2026-08-28 reproduces all 12 fields of the original artifact. 2026-08-26, 2026-08-27 and 2026-08-29 then give the same pool of 108, 0 never served and 108 served (`POOL-ELEGIVEL-2026-08-26-to-29.json`). The set of pool ids is identical (same hash) in copies frozen on 2026-08-26, 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-07. A copy frozen on 2026-09-08, after the corpus was re-ingested, fails the control (pool 55) and is not used. Limit: importance and pain are read as stored in those copies, so they bracket the four days rather than observe each instant.

findings.quote_pt: **Por que isso é resultado e não nota de rodapé:** a renovação da superfície não é governada por relevância nem pelo ranker. É governada por quais **caminhos de arquivo** o canal foi configurado para enxergar — e o corpus cresceu para fora deles.
findings.problem: §4.3.1 decomposes only the coverage channel. The main pool (8 of 10 slots) gets no per-filter decomposition, so «policy, not capacity» is assumed for it (open item 6). Insert the paragraph and table below right after this passage, before the 'counting trap' note.
findings.proposed_en:
**The main pool, filter by filter.** The main pool reaches its 8 slots through seven serial stages (`brief.ts:202-215, 371-397, 420-468, 819-821`): (F1) routing, where the agent sub-pool sees only `sessions/<agent>/%` with quota 5 and the `scope=global` sub-pool sees the whole corpus; (F2) a `since` window, inactive because production sends none; (F3) a SQL proxy pre-rank with `LIMIT 500` per sub-pool; (F4) the exact `calculateSalience` re-rank; (F5) dedup by id, exact title/one-liner and near-duplicate containment ≥ 0.6; (F6) quotas capped at `mainTarget = n − freshSlots = 8`; and (F7) the high-pain floor, which picks first the items of the no-fresh brief with `pain ≥ 0.9`. We reimplemented them on the frozen corpus of these days (`p2-ord-ro-2026-08-26.db`, 67,187 chunks). The reconstruction reproduces the served main slots in **100%** of the 672 briefs of each day from 24/08 to 07/09. Counting exclusions is the wrong instrument here: F3 alone removes 95.7% of the corpus from candidacy and binds nothing. The question is answered by lifting **one** filter at a time and recomputing every brief:

| lifted | briefs whose main set changes (of 672) | distinct main chunks per day |
|---|---:|---:|
| none (as served) | — | **33** |
| F1 routing | 672 | **8** |
| F2 `since` | — (inactive) | 33 |
| F3 `LIMIT 500` | **0** | 33 |
| F4 exact re-rank | 672 | 33 |
| F5 dedup | 192 | 33 |
| F6 quota split | 672 | **8** |
| F7 high-pain floor | 672 | 33 |

No filter, lifted, widens the surface; the two that change its breadth **narrow** it, because routing by agent is the main pool's only source of variety. The breadth is exactly `3 + 6 agents × 5`: the 3 shared slots are taken by the high-pain floor (chunks 112241, 116107 and 116467, `pain = 1.0`, in every brief), and each agent gets the same 5 in every brief. A day has **5,376** main slots and they serve **33** distinct chunks, which is 0.61% of the slot capacity and 163 serves per chunk. These are the same 33 on every measurable day from 21/08 to 21/09, and the serving log alone, without the database, gives 37 for the whole month. A rotation over the same slots could serve 5,376 distinct chunks a day, or 8.0% of the corpus. So the main pool is **not** capacity-bound at the day, the unit at which §4.1 measures exposure. It is bound by its ranking: a deterministic top-k with no serve-history term, removed on purpose on 2026-06-26 (`brief.ts:786-792`). Both channels are therefore governed by policy rather than by slots, but by **different** policies. The coverage channel exhausts an eligibility predicate of 108 chunks; the main pool returns the same arg-max for the same route, with 99.95% of the corpus admitted to the ranking and never reached. Daily, the two surfaces are disjoint and add up to the whole: 33 + 108 = **141** distinct chunks, every day from 24/08 to 19/09.
